text: The written account says Yahweh told Abram to leave his country and his father's house. Abram was to go to a land that Yahweh would show him. Yahweh promised to make of him a great nation.
The written account says Abram was very rich. He had livestock, silver and gold.
Abram lived in the land of Canaan, and Lot lived in the cities of the plain. Lot moved his tent as far as Sodom.
Abraham split the wood for the offering and went to the place God had told him about. On the third day, he looked up and saw the place far off.
God said that all the nations of the earth would be blessed through Abraham's offspring. Then Abraham returned to his young men, and they went together to Beersheba.

The written account says Joseph was seventeen years old when he was feeding the flock with his brothers. Their father Israel loved Joseph more than all his children and made him a coat of many colors.
The written account says Yahweh spoke to Moses and Aaron in Egypt. He said this month would be the first month of the year to them.
Each family's lamb had to be without defect, a male a year old. They kept it until the fourteenth day of the month.
Israel was told to take some of the lamb's blood and put it on the two door posts and the lintel of their houses.
Israel was to eat the Passover meal ready to go. They wore belts on their waists and shoes on their feet, with a staff in the hand. They ate it in haste.
Moses stretched out his hand over the sea. Yahweh caused the sea to go back by a strong east wind all night. The waters were divided, and the sea became dry land.
The people called the food manna. It was white like coriander seed, and it tasted like wafers with honey. They ate it for forty years, until they came to the borders of Canaan.
Goliath of Gath, the Philistine champion, was six cubits and a span tall. He wore a brass helmet and a coat of mail that weighed five thousand shekels.
David took his staff in his hand and chose five smooth stones out of the brook. He put them in the pouch of his shepherd's bag.
The house that King Solomon built for Yahweh was sixty cubits long, twenty cubits wide and thirty cubits high.
King Solomon spent seven years building the house of Yahweh. In the end it was finished throughout all its parts, just as planned.

The queen of Sheba heard about Solomon's fame and came to test him with hard questions. She came to Jerusalem with a very great caravan, with camels carrying spices, a lot of gold and precious stones.
Once every three years the fleet of Tarshish came to King Solomon. It brought gold, silver, ivory, apes and peacocks.
Babylon was an ancient city on the Euphrates river in Mesopotamia. Its ruins are in Iraq, about 53 mi (85 km) south of Baghdad.
Babylon may have been the first city with more than 200,000 people. It covered an area of about 3.5 sq mi (900 ha).
The Ishtar Gate was 49 ft (15 m) high, and its foundations went another 46 ft (14 m) underground.
The Processional Way ran through the Ishtar Gate. Its walls showed about 120 lions, bulls, dragons and flowers on yellow and black glazed bricks.
The Hanging Gardens of Babylon were one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World. They were described as rising tiers of gardens with many trees, shrubs and vines, like a large green mountain.
The written account says Daniel was taken up out of the den of lions. No kind of harm was found on him, because he had trusted in his God.
At its peak, the Persian empire covered about 2.1 million sq mi (5.5 million square kilometers). It was the largest empire of its time.
Under Darius the Great, the empire stretched from Southeast Europe and Northeast Africa in the west to the Indus Valley in the east.
Cyrus is honored in Judaism for freeing the Jewish people from captivity in Babylon. He did it by issuing the Edict of Restoration.
According to the Book of Isaiah, Yahweh anointed Cyrus for this task and called him a messiah. Cyrus is the only non-Jewish person honored in this way.
Mounted couriers were supposed to travel the 1,677 miles (2,699 km) from Susa to Sardis in nine days. On foot the trip took ninety days.
The Royal Road was built for fast communication across the western part of the empire, from Susa to Sardis. It was probably perfected under Darius I.
The Phoenicians were an ancient people who lived in city-states along the eastern Mediterranean coast. Most of their land was in what is now Lebanon.
The Phoenicians traded all over the Mediterranean Sea. They went from Cyprus to the Iberian Peninsula. They left thousands of inscriptions.
Tyre juts out from the coast of the Mediterranean Sea, about 50 mi (80 km) south of Beirut. It is one of the oldest cities in the world that people have lived in without a break.
The Phoenician alphabet was one of the first alphabets. It was written horizontally, from right to left, and was the first to have a fixed writing direction.
The Phoenician alphabet used one symbol for each sound. That meant there were only a few dozen symbols to learn.
The Phoenician alphabet used 22 letters, all of them consonants. It left the vowel sounds for the reader to supply.
